CONCLUSIONS In this project we built, calibrated, and validated a hierarchical macro–micro finite-element framework that links HPDC Aural-5 (Al7SiMgMn) microstructure to fracture response under three-point bending and clinch loading—the two tests most relevant to SPR performance. Phase I established the end-to-end workflow: macro models to localize failure-prone regions and extract deformation histories; micro-models that explicitly represent Al-dendrites and Al/Si eutectics; and data-driven calibration of phase properties and fracture strains using tensile data, inverse nano-indentation, RVEs, and 3-P bending. The calibrated e- coat micro-model reproduced the measured clinch critical displacement and was further checked against VDA bending, providing strong validation. Phase II leveraged these foundations to quantify how casting- condition–controlled features (e.g., dendrite/eutectic morphology and e-coat–induced nano-precipitates) govern rivetability, and to develop a reduced-order model for rapid microstructure screening. Collectively, the results provide a predictive route to specify casting and e-coating windows that achieve target SPR performance, enable substitution of energy-intensive solution treatments with low-energy HT or the design of NHT alloys, and support the adoption of super-large, thin-wall HPDC body structures for lighter, more efficient EVs. The development in this project enable us to deploy the macro-micro approach to formulate practical design rules and extend the approach to additional alloys and joint geometries in future work. 7.
